text:
mari: Heads-up — onboarding cust Lumina's adapter (delta-adapter v2.1). Quick smoke: quantized int4 path is weirdly shifting numbers on invoice samples. anyone seen this pattern before?

linus: saw a similar offset on another customer's adapter last month, but that was token remap mismatch, not quant bleed. can you paste a failing example?

mari: sure — short sample below (redacted):

```
input: \"Invoice total: $1,020.50\"
expected: \"Total amount: $1,020.50\"
model (int4): \"Total amount: $1020.5\"  <-- decimal truncated in parsing step
```

sasha: hmm that looks like a tokenizer detokenization rounding thing. which tokenizer did you pin in the merge config?

mari: adapter merge config uses tokenizer: cust-lumina-vocab-1 + base tokeniser en-v2 (we grafted vocab entries).

linus: grafting custom vocab can cause subtokens to merge differently under quant. Try re-running with the adapter applied but forcing the base tokenizer only (no graft) to confirm.

mari: running now: `./evalpack-lite --samples 100 --mode=canary --quant=int4` — kicked off. eval-bot will post results.

eval-bot: quick results (canary): 100 samples complete. 8/100 show decimal formatting diffs; 2 are full numeric dropouts. latency +5% vs fp16 baseline. see CI: https://ci.internal.redwood/run/7832

sasha: can you dump tokens for one bad sample? `model.tokenize(...)` output + detokenized steps.

mari: pasted one below:

```
# token ids (grafted)
[101, 2020, 3456, 9999, 402, 5002, 11]
# detok before postproc:
"Total amount: 1 020 . 5 0"
# postproc joins -> "1,020.50"
# int4 path produced "1020.5"
```

linus: interesting — detok inserted spaces between subtoken groups, postproc usually cleans but int4 path seems to drop the trailing 0. could be quantized softmax precision causing beam scoring to prefer a shorter token sequence.

mari: repro note: only happens when adapter is merged with grafted tokens + int4 quant. fp16 and int8-ok.

sasha: two actionable checks: 1) re-run with `--force-postproc` to ensure postprocessing applied in the runtime path; 2) run a tiny beam-size=1 vs beam=5 comparison to see if scoring differs.

mari: started beam tests and `--force-postproc`. Will update when CI finishes.

deploy-bot: canary deployment for cust-lumina/delta-adapter-v2.1 triggered on host stack-5 at 1783219905.

mari: quick update: `--force-postproc` fixed 6/8 cases; remaining 2 still drop 0. beam=5 recovered one of them. So scoring is definitely involved.

linus: sounds like combined effect: grafted subtokens + quant noise shifts marginal logit such that shorter numeric token wins. Mitigation options: 1) bias numeric tokens by small additive logit on the decoder for known numeric spans, 2) adjust quant calibration to preserve numeric token logits, 3) recommend using int8 for this customer for now.

sasha: for rollout plan, propose: canary -> metric: numeric-format-accuracy >= 99.5% on invoice set. If not met, pin to int8 and schedule a calibration sweep for int4.

mari: agreed. I'll open an eval ticket with the invoice testset, attach token dumps, and add calibration run. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-1248

eval-bot: created artifact: s3://redwood-eval/cust-lumina/delta-v2.1/1783219876/ — includes logs, token dumps, evalpack results.

linus: thanks. Also add a small unit test in the merge pipeline to run these numeric-format checks on graft merges to catch regressions before canary.

mari: adding that to the merge CI now. will ping when done. :thumbsup:

sasha: great, thanks. feel free to escalate if calibration sweep needs infra quota.

mari: will do. closing thread once patch lands.
